topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes, connects them to prior histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Discovery and laboratory assays of viral transformation and oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor-transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and how their transforming properties are assayed experimentally in the laboratory.

topics.label: Functional classifications and molecular dynamics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define and illustrate how oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations alter gene function and cell cycle control through dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mechanisms.

topics.label: Mechanisms and progression of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular defects in DNA repair, replication, and chromosome segregation that generate sequence and chromosomal instability and drive multistep tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predispositions and genetic instability in tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how germline mutations in tumor suppressor and caretaker genes predispose individuals to cancer and explore the dynamics of genetic instability during tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes, recommending supplementary reading, and previewing the next session.
